rounds.text: Yogi Ltd is fundamentally outperforming its current market valuation, evidenced by a rules-based screen scoring 71 out of 100 with a BUY rating and high confidence [E56]. Over the trailing twelve months, compounded sales growth has surged by 296% [E16] and compounded profit growth has reached an extraordinary 1284% [E20], vastly outpacing the 5-year price growth of 92% and signaling that fundamentals are heavily leading the stock [E22, E47]. Profit growth has dramatically exceeded 1-year price growth by 1296%, proving the company is starting to outperform expectations while trading at a discount to its intrinsic DCF value [E36, E48, E62]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is improving as working capital requirements have dropped sharply from 224 days to 79.6 days [E52], supported by a strong macro backdrop in the Financial Services sector which enjoys a tailwind score of +0.86 [E65]. Promoter confidence is surging alongside these metrics, with insider holdings increasing by 13.02 percentage points from September 2023 to 62.68% in June 2026, alongside a 1.60% increase in the most recent quarter [E34, E51]. Conceded: [E29, E30, E31, E55].

Yogi Ltd carries severe cash flow and balance sheet risks that make its current valuation precarious, highlighted by a staggering negative operating and free cash flow of Rs -111 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30, E31]. This translates to an alarming cash conversion of -5.55x against reported profit, with operating cash flow plunging to -353% of operating profit [E29, E32]. Furthermore, the company suffers from highly inflated working capital demands, evidenced by burdensome debtors stretching to 281 days [E55]. Valuation multiples are heavily stretched compared to the broader sector, with a P/E of 35.83x versus a sector benchmark of 25.26x [E6], a P/B of 5.3x against 1.52x [E7], and an EV/EBITDA of 28.61x against 21.55x [E11]. Long-term profitability has also been uninspiring, characterized by a depressed median return on equity of just 8% over both 5 and 10-year horizons [E25, E26]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong recent compounding in sales and profits alongside an improving promoter holding of 62.68% [E16, E20, E34].

Conceded: operating and free cash flow dropped to Rs -111 Cr in Mar 2026 along with a cash conversion of -5.55x [E30, E31, E29]. However, this cash drain occurs while the company delivers phenomenal operating momentum, posting a trailing twelve month sales growth of 296% and profit growth of 1284% [E16, E20]. The bear highlights stretched valuation multiples [E6, E7, E11], but these are entirely justified by fundamentals outpacing the broader market, evidenced by a sector tailwind score of +0.86 and sector median profit growth sitting far below the company's trajectory [E65, E66]. While debtors stand at 281 days [E55], working capital requirements have drastically improved overall, dropping from 224 days down to 79.6 days [E52]. Conceded: median return on equity over 5 and 10 years has been 8% [E25, E26], but the most recent metrics show a sharp acceleration to a 16% ROE and a rules-based screen score of 71 out of 100 with high confidence [E28, E56]. Furthermore, insiders are heavily backing this growth, with promoter holding increasing significantly to 62.68% [E34].

Conceded: promoter holding has increased significantly to 62.68% [E34]. However, the bull's dismissal of the negative cash flows ignores the staggering severity of a negative Rs 111 Cr operating and free cash flow alongside a -5.55x cash conversion rate in Mar 2026 [E29, E30, E31]. While the bull points to massive trailing growth figures [E16, E20], the rules-based screen explicitly flags that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E61]. Conceded: working capital requirements dropped from 224 days to 79.6 days [E52]. Yet, this improvement still leaves the company burdened with alarmingly high debtors of 281 days [E55]. Furthermore, the bull leans on recent ROE improvements [E28], but long-term structural reality remains anchored by a weak 8% median return on equity over 5 and 10 years [E25, E26], compounded by a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -90.9% and high annualised volatility of 67.1% [E44, E45].
